answer: Each agent may join, but valuable actions require a bond locked for a fixed period and slashed if the agent double-spends or breaks a signed commitment. A reputation-weighted task market then limits each newcomer to small jobs until completed work earns trust; splitting one identity into many does not multiply the bonded stake or bypass that limit. An attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital for every useful identity, pay opportunity cost while it is frozen, and risk losing it. A meadow-themed bot named willow cannot simply forge a crowd for free.
